newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil steady on physical buys.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil steady on physical buys.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady at midday on Tuesday as the market looked to sustained physical support to offset any large arbitrage exports from the West, traders said.
"The market is steady this morning because of the physical buying yesterday and talks of refinery shutdowns," one trader said.
June gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.20/$25.30 per barrel while July was at $25.10/$25.20, both largely unchanged from Monday's quotes, brokers said.

Traders said swap prices were steady despite reports of exports of up to 250,000 tonnes of gas oil from the Black Sea and Mediterranean to Asia due to market perception of sustained buying from some traders.

Industry sources estimate that four tankers of between 60,000 and 80,000 tonnes have been fixed for shipment to the East, with others estimating as many as seven to eight tankers due for arrival in early July.
Traders said the market is not discounting another round of large purchases from the group of three traders who have since March 3 bought about 22 million barrels of gas oil.

One of the traders bought a 150,000 barrel cargo on Monday for June 28-July 2 loading at $25.35 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, up about 50 cents from last Thursday. This reflected stronger price levels in the forward weeks with cargoes for the earlier weeks seen at lower values.
Industry sources said aside from the physical support from these traders, the market is also looking to the re-emergence of enduser buying from China, Indonesia and India.

China halved its April gas oil imports over March to around 400,000 tonnes and is also said to have bought similar amounts in May and the low purchases are also expected to be extended to June, traders said.
China had reduced its second quarter imports due to high stocks, port congestion and large impors in the first quarter.
Traders said China is likely to raise its imports for July delivery after the high stocks are run down.

Indonesia is expected to raise its imports in July due to the scheduled shutdown of a 200,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit at the 265,000-bpd Balikpapan refinery for one month from July 10.
India has raised its July imports to 855,000 tonnes from 315,000 tonnes in June.
June fuel oil swaps were last quoted steady at $100.50/$101.50.
